quest.title: The Sea of Fog and the Rite of the Trees
quest.description: After passing the Maushiro to Sumida, the nature of your commission changes to exploring and investigating Tsurumi Island further. Considering that illusion of Kama you saw, you might need to ask the real one about a few things. With any luck, you might still find him in Ritou.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Hero's Wit x3, Mora x30000, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: What's the matter?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We ran into some very concerning things on Tsurumi Island...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Your point being?

choices.text: We'd like to know what your relationship with the island is.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: That's none of your business.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: You've already helped Lady Sumida find the Maushiro, so there is no need for any further association between us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yikes, how cold. Actually, Miss Sumida's commission isn't over yet. She wanted us to continue investigating Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Alright. I understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? And now he's so willing all of a sudden...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: "Kama" is my family's... Just consider it my clan's name. Our ancestor was from Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What!? Why didn't Miss Sumida tell us any of that?

choices.text: Gasp! Shock! Lightning crackle, lightning crackle!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: That's because I never told her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But why—

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Because she never asked. If she asked, I would have told her. But since she hasn't, I'm simply her boatman.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I follow her to Yashiori Island to gather reference material. I smuggle snacks from Liyue. I listen to her read books. I think this is a good deal.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: My ancestor could not stomach what was happening on Tsurumi Island and left.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: So he built a small boat and followed the path of the so-called Thunderbird.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: That's right.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: My ancestors lived on Seirai Island for a long time. Some time later, the Thunderbird destroyed Tsurumi Island, and even later on, it was killed on Seirai. The island became nigh-uninhabitable then, so we migrated to Kannazuka.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Asase Shrine was constructed to suppress the Thunderbird's power, or so I heard, while Koseki Village was built to house those who had relocated to Seirai to make offerings at the shrine.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Our family was lucky enough to survive these various catastrophes, and so we began working in Tatarasuna. Afterward, having despaired of the way in which the then-inspector acted, my ancestors resigned and moved to Narukami Island.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Previously, we even made a tidy sum of Mora in Ritou doing business... but by the time it came to my father's generation, we had little to our name but a pile of debts.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: You really remember history very clearly...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Each generation of our family will tell our story to the one that follows. We have a strong oral tradition.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It is said that this was due to our earliest ancestor claiming that he had given up everything — save for the reason he had left in the first place.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Before my father passed on, he claimed that we were the last scions of the people of Tsurumi Island, although that hardly counts for much.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: We were no illustrious clan, like one might consider the Hiiragi or Kamisato to be. The only thing he left to me was a single small boat.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Why did your ancestor leave Tsurumi Island?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: We hold that it is because the Thunderbird showed favor to a certain child, which the priests then decided to sacrifice to it.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Our ancestor could not accept such a thing, so he left. He originally wanted to take the child with him, but it seems that the other party stayed of their own accord.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That must've been really hard for him...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So the unnatural occurrences on the island...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: They must be the result of very large-scale ley line disorder. It is said that the sound of Tsurumi Island being destroyed could be heard all the way from Seirai.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Was the Thunderbird really that powerful?

choices.text: Considering that it could reduce Seirai Island to such a state...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: My father did take me to Tsurumi once, to "see where it all began."

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Apparitions of the past would appear amidst the Sea of Fog, illusions replaying past events — namely, the final ceremony held on the island, albeit one in which the flow of time is all wrong.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: The Thunderbird then destroyed Tsurumi Island, resulting in a great storm... and then it started all over again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So that's the reason why those people didn't take any notice of us at all? Because they were all illusions of the past?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: There's no meaning in speaking to the islanders. They are simply shadows created by the ley line disorders.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: However, there is one exception, which is the child who was the offering to the Thunderbird. I believe this to be the "Ruu" you spoke of.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... But... That means we've got to save him!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I wouldn't worry about this. They are all ultimately illusions created by the ley lines.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, so the whole "Ghost Maushiro" thing Miss Sumida talked about was true!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...But never mind all that! Paimon thinks we should at least try to help Ruu!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even if he is an illusion, he's still Paimon's friend.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Mm. Well, it doesn't matter to me either way. I have no love for Tsurumi, nor do I have any for my father's talk of bloodlines and history.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Hmm, if I were Lady Sumida, I would say something like: "If the cycle of the Sea of Fog can be broken, then that 'history' may also be ended."

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Haha, very funny.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But you didn't laugh...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Really? I did, in fact, find it quite interesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: W—Well, sure... Either way, thanks for telling us all this stuff, Kama!

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Lady Sumida commissioned you.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I have said enough, I believe.

choices.text: I'd like to help him, too.
I'd like to explore the island further, too.
I'm afraid it is that powerful, Paimon.
I'm guessing she doesn't know either.
Miss Sumida would like to know more about your relation to Tsurumi Island.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Alright. I understand.

talks.objective: Go to Tsurumi Island and look for Ruu
Go to Tsurumi Island and look for Ruu

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Isn't Ruu lucky~

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: Don't be silly.

dialogues.speaker: Makiri
dialogues.text: Oh. Sorry.

dialogues.speaker: Ipe
dialogues.text: And the fact that I'm the only one doing work over here makes it worse!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's Ipe and Makiri. Looks like they're making offerings to the Perch.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh... Paimon has an idea.

choices.text: What a coincidence. So do I.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They said that the Perches are key to the ceremony, and so people need to make offerings there and protect them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, the ceremony won't be able to continue if we destroy the Perches, right?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But they're illusions of the past...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, even if that's so, don't you think it's worth a shot?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Since these islanders love their Thunderbird and perches and stuff so much, let's just give wrecking 'em a go!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: They said that these perches contain the Thunderbird's power, right? Maybe they'll react if we blow them away...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu's not here...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Maybe he's deeper inside.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We need to find him, and quick! If not, the islanders are gonna sacrifice him to the Thunderbird!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: According to what Kama said...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, Paimon knows that all the things happening here are illusions that constantly repeat themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if that's the case... doesn't that mean that Ruu's been sacrificed to the Thunderbird Archon-only-knows how many times?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's... That's just too sad! We've got to help him, no matter what!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You're right. Let's do this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah!

talks.objective: Talk to the people of Tsurumi Island

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Ah, it's you two...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Have there been any new developments?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Mm, I've got it. Now, let's break this down simply...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: According to your plot, the flow of time in Tsurumi Island does not match that of the outside world. If it were me, I certainly would — as you have — ascribed this to a special ley line disorder.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I doubt that such a ley line disorder could occur naturally, so... Let's just say it fell from the skies? Maybe it was a fragment of Celestia, or something...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Which then mixed together with the lightning storms created by the Thunderbird to create these phenomena—

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: —And I'd give this plot a 4 out of 10, maybe. It's usable, but it's hard to execute. There should be a more elegant way of writing this...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you mean when you say "plot," anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about it. It's nothing of particular note...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: So if we want to push the story forward, we need a few more plot points in play — for example... "The Tsurumi tragedy was born from a misunderstanding."

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: That's what I'd write, anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: For example, the priests and Ruu might have taken the Thunderbird's favor upon Ruu as a sign that it wanted him as a sacrifice, but in truth, the Thunderbird might have just liked him in particular.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I suppose the resolution to such a plotline would simply be to find a way to convey Ruu's feelings to the Thunderbird.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, I can't say for sure, but I don't think there's any problem with this progression, per se. I remember a very popular series that ran for at least a few dozen volumes with this plot as the basis for its story!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: You just need to find some ways to continuously insert various happenings that pose obstacles to the misunderstanding's resolution and allow it to fester! Why, that book...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Could we get back on topic?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Oh. Right. Sorry...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: But according to the developments you've mentioned, since the Thunderbird was vanquished on Seirai Island, and Ruu himself is but a shade of the past, then you can only avert this catastrophe via some mystical means.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmmm, this... This really is quite hard to write. There are so many things that would be hard to explain. Unacceptable. "The Chronicles of the Sea of Fog (Working Title)" can't be that sort of story...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #Do you have any other ideas, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Mind if we say something about Kama for a moment?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Oh, you've seen him around, then?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...Wait, what? Kama is a descendant of Tsurumi Island's natives?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: L—Let's go look for him — right now!

choices.text: Don't you think that's rather cliché?

talks.objective: Search for the Perch's scattered power

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That should be all of those perches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let's hope that's enough to stop the ceremony.

choices.text: Well, let's just hope so, eh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We've got no clue where Ruu is...

choices.text: Well, if we want to be sure that we've disrupted the ceremony...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's right! Ruu always wanted us to take part in that ceremony...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's hope it doesn't end the same way this time.

choices.text: We should go to the ceremonial site.
It's all in the past now, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon knows that! But...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ruu! You're alright...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: Why... Why did you do this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh?

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: I thought that the two of you were good, strong people...

dialogues.speaker: Ruu
dialogues.text: And that you'd be different from the others! You came back to look for me, listened to everything I said... I thought that the ceremony would go well this time... But...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We want to stop the ceremony! That way, you'll be safe!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But you're not helping!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Back then... Something happened. Something went wrong. Things were going so well...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But then I woke up. I found that the island had become like this. Everyone was weird. No one could see me. No one could hear me!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Then after a while, a storm would start, and it would be super scary. At these times, only Wakukau, Oina, and Autake wouldn't be struck by lightning. I'd hide there and wait for the storm to end.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: But once the thunder stopped, everything would repeat all over again. I would wake up — and everyone would be doing the same things.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Kapatcir's missing, too. I couldn't find her, not even on Mt. Kanna.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: The ceremony must have gone wrong. We must've made her angry.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That's why I prepared another ceremony, and another, and another. But it always ends the same. That's why I had the idea of bringing in people from the outside.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: I thought that... you were my friends, and that you'd help me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, hold on a moment. Who is Kapatcir, anyway?

choices.text: That's what I've been thinking, too.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Other people call her the Thunderbird. She's our guardian deity.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: If the ceremony goes smoothly, Kapatcir will be pleased. That way, everyone will be happy.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: In the past, Kapatcir paid no attention to the people who were offered to her. But I'm different...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That's why I have to make sure that the ceremony goes well. That way, everyone can go back to normal and live their lives again.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Big Brother Ipe and Big Sister Makiri will get married, and Kina and Kito will grow up and become great adventurers!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: And once things are better here, Big Sister Sayo will come back! Big Brother Kama, too! And Dad will no longer have to be afraid of Kapatcir's wrathful lightning!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: And everyone would realize that the outside world isn't a bad place, because there are good people like you in it...

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: ...So why? Why did you ruin the ceremony?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Because this isn't right!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That's not true! This is right! Don't... Don't come back here again!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: There's going to be another storm. I—It's going to be super scary!

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: Just go already! I don't want to see you ever again! *sobs*

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Mm. You're... You're right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go.

choices.text: Let's go and report back to Miss Sumida.

response.speaker: Ruu
response.text: That's right, that's what they call her. She's our guardian deity.

choices.text: Why do you want the ceremony to proceed?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! It works! It really works!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: C'mon, let's go get the rest!

choices.text: The ceremony is past tense, you know...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we've met Ruu, haven't we? That isn't something that happened in the past.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's keep going!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Th—That was close!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We barely managed to get out...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—So this is the storm that Kama talked about...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It could've been a result of us destroying the Perches.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true. They did have power in them after all...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh-oh! If it's storming out there, Ruu might be in danger...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Maybe, but... Paimon's still worried.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, let's double back and see if we can find him, then.

choices.text: I'm not sure we'll be able to find him.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It'll be hard, yeah, but we should go check on him anyway.

choices.text: We should go look for him.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Indulge my curiosity for a moment... Since you're a descendant of Tsurumi Island's people and your family seems quite interested in handing down their history...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Would you know how to make Maushiro, by any chance, Kama?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: It's totally okay if you don't, by the way! It was a long time ago and all...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: I do. My grandfather taught me how to make them — and how to use them, too.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: What... Uh... Then why did I spend all that Mora to hire people...

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: *cough* So then, is there anything else you can tell me about the Maushiro?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: They make "bwoooom" sounds.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: I—I think I already knew that. Is there anything else?

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: They are made of wood, and have no special requirements in that regard. Yumemiru Wood, Otogi Wood, they will all do.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Let me think, was there anything else... Ah. If you give a Maushiro you made personally to someone, that is considered a marriage proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: That's not bad, actually. I'll include that into the story!

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: All that talking has tired me out.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Best of luck to you.

talks.objective: Go to Tsurumi Island and look for Ruu once again

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: #...It is as {NICKNAME} says. I am a descendant of the Tsurumi Island natives.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: Why didn't you tell me that earlier? All those times I got you to send those people there...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: You never asked, Lady Sumida.

dialogues.speaker: Sumida
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, that is just how you are, but...

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: Nor will telling Tsurumi's story edify anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: My father clung to that story till his dying day. From the time I was young, he would often take me there. It's a gloomy place, one filled with nothing but terrible memories.

dialogues.speaker: Kama
dialogues.text: But had you asked me, Lady Sumida, I would have told you.

choices.text: You should have a bit more faith in him.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...You're right. If I had been more willing to ask for his opinion and trusted him more, I wouldn't have had to do this in such a roundabout fashion.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I'm sorry, Kama.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It's alright.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: W—Well then, as a remnant of Tsurumi Island, what do you think of this? "The last scion of Tsurumi returns to his desolate homeland, only to be caught up in the twisted weft of time..."

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Simply put, you hear the call of your ancestors and head into the mists of Tsurumi Island. Following the sound of the Maushiro, you traverse the fog, only to realize as you approach the site of that millennia-old ceremony...

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: ...That you've become the same ancestor who bore your name all those years ago! There, you experience the island's final day — until violet lightning and roaring thunder rend the skies!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Then you awake — only to have the same day begin again!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well, what do you think? Is this plot "This Novel Is Amazing!" grand prize-worthy?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Will this really work...?

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: It's not that impressive.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Hmm, I get it, I get it. You probably greatly value Tsurumi's history, so it's no surprise that you might be offended by my fictional appropriations. So, how about this, then...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I'm not talking about that. Tsurumi's history doesn't matter that much to me.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: I just feel that this plot doesn't grab me as much as the "Toki Alley Tales" or "Kino's Travels" that you read to me before. Nor does it quite flow as freely as "The Three Young Nobles."

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Uh... Um, that was... blunt of you.

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Sorry.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: N—No, don't apologize at moments like this. That just feels even more hurtful to me as a writer...

response.speaker: Kama
response.text: Sorry, I shouldn't have apologized.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Aghhh! This is so annoying — but most annoying of all is the fact that I can't refute your critique.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Yes, I know. I will do that. Kama's heard a lot of stories, after all. If he finds them interesting, I'm sure my editor will, too!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Paimon... was just thinking.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's never giving up, mind you! Paimon's just thinking... Could we try the method that Miss Sumida just mentioned?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Eh? What did I say? I've already forgotten...

choices.text: We could give it a go...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But you're the one who said not to give up, {NICKNAME}! Paimon won't, either!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And anyway, didn't we agree to go have a good meal at Kiminami Restaurant once we finish this commission?

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: I don't think I follow, exactly, but it's good to see that Paimon's so spirited.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, you're talking to the illustrious Paimon, after all!

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Well then, about this commission of ours...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll continue plumbing the depths of Tsurumi Island's mysteries.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: Alright. In that case, I look forward to your next report.

response.speaker: Sumida
response.text: #How do you adventurers say it again? Ah, right. "Ad astra abyssosque," {NICKNAME}!

choices.text: I wouldn't get my hopes up.
You just need to write something that Kama will find interesting.
